6.15 The Silent-Ignore Cohort — The Scoreboard Records Hits but Never Records Misses

Ten dome predictions have now had their declared test windows close with no result ever posted on the dome's own predictions page. The model promotes confirmations into its headline “WIN” tally but leaves expired and failed predictions sitting indefinitely as pending, so the public scoreboard structurally counts hits and cannot count misses. This is not an accusation of bad faith — it is a measurable asymmetry in the dome's own published record (data/predictions.json; data/sections.json:p6-612-11).

The plain-English problem

A prediction is only worth something if the same scoreboard that records its success also records its failure. The dome's predictions page does the first and not the second. When a registered prediction is confirmed, the dome can fold it into the headline count of claimed wins on wins.html; when a registered prediction's test window closes with no supporting result, nothing happens — the entry simply remains marked pending on the dome's side, often for over a month past the window it set for itself. Across the ten predictions tracked here, the dome has posted a result for exactly zero of them after their windows closed (data/predictions.json:PRED-073; data/predictions.json:PRED-105). The scoreboard only moves in one direction.

This is the operational complement to the structural critique in Section 6.12, which showed that the April 2026 closure cluster produced zero dome-discriminating confirmations across eleven windows (data/sections.json:p6-612-11). Section 6.12 asked “did any closed prediction actually distinguish the dome from standard physics?” and answered no. This section asks the narrower bookkeeping question — “when a window closes without a confirmation, does the dome ever record that?” — and the answer is also no. A model that can register a prediction publicly but has no mechanism to register its own miss is not running a falsification test; it is running an advertising funnel where only positive outcomes are ever surfaced.

The silent-ignore cohort

Each row below is a dome prediction whose self-declared test window has closed with no result posted by the author. “Dome status” is the author-side posture in the dome's own record (or our reconstruction of it where the dome leaves the entry untouched); “Our verdict” is this review's independent scientific assessment, which does not depend on the dome ever posting anything.

Scoreboard tally: ten closed windows, zero dome-posted results. By our independent assessment the column resolves to seven standard_physics/recycled restatements of phenomena that were already settled at registration, two tacit_withdrawal entries past the 14-day silence rule, and one falsified (PRED-073). None resolves to a dome-discriminating confirmation. The dome's headline win count, by contrast, has continued to grow over the same period.

* Fairness caveat for PRED-073

Our falsified verdict on PRED-073 rests on the secular-rate null, not on a post-window observation. The dome cited CHAOS-7 as its verification source, but CHAOS-7's final data release predates the test window and CHAOS-8 coverage ends in 2025 — no published CHAOS release yet covers April–May 2026 (data/predictions.json:PRED-073). The falsification therefore follows from the dome committing to ≥0.3°/month when the well-measured IGRF-13/CHAOS-7 western-cell rate is 0.282°/year (~0.024° over the window), which trips the dome's own published <0.1° falsification threshold (Finlay et al. 2020, Earth Planets Space 72:156, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9). We flag this honestly: PRED-073 is “falsified on the dome's own rule under the consensus null,” not “falsified by a fresh contradicting measurement,” and we do not count it as a confirmed observational miss until a future CHAOS-8 update lands. Even excluding PRED-073 entirely, the cohort is nine closed windows with zero dome-posted results.

Author-status standardization

The dome leaves stale entries marked pending indefinitely, which over-counts “live” predictions and obscures the silence. To keep our own catalog honest rather than mirror the dome's bookkeeping, this review standardizes the author-side status of any prediction whose window closed 14 or more days ago with no posted result. Eight entries (PRED-087, 088, 111, 085, 077, 090, 081, 106 — all closed 2026-04-30, now 39 days silent) are recommended to move from pending to dome_silent_terminal, the same terminal-silence status already assigned to PRED-105 under the 14-day rule (data/predictions.json:PRED-105). We deliberately reconcile the originating proposal's requested label “silent_ignore_confirmed” onto the existing dome_silent_terminal value rather than introduce a fourth silence vocabulary — the taxonomy already distinguishes transient silence (dome_silent) from terminal silence (dome_silent_terminal), and adding a synonym would fragment it. PRED-073 (8 days) stays dome_silent until it crosses the 14-day threshold; PRED-105 is unchanged. This standardization touches author-side status only and changes none of our independent verdicts.

Kernel of truth

The dome gets something genuinely right that most fringe models never attempt: it registers falsifiable, numerically-specific predictions in public, with declared test windows and explicit falsification thresholds, and it timestamps them. PRED-073 in particular is a textbook-clean prospective claim — a committed magnitude, a committed direction, a committed window, and the author's own falsification rule written down in advance. That is more methodological discipline than the vast majority of alternative-cosmology projects ever show, and we credit it. The failure is not in making predictions; it is in the asymmetric accounting that follows. Registration creates an obligation to post the result either way, and the dome discharges that obligation only when the result is favorable. A genuine falsification program would have a “misses” column on its own scoreboard. The dome has the prediction-registration half of the scientific method and is missing the result-posting half — and it is precisely the missing half that converts a list of guesses into a track record.

Anticipated objections

“The predictions are still pending — the data may not be in yet.” For the geodetic, seismic, tidal, and supernova entries (PRED-087, 088, 111, 085, 077, 081) the relevant datasets — GRACE/GRACE-FO geoid and mascon products, IRIS seismic catalogs, NOAA tide-gauge records, JWST supernova photometry — were public and complete well before the registration date of 2026-04-04; these restate measurements that already existed, so “data not in yet” does not apply (data/sections.json:p6-612-11). For PRED-106 the missing data is an experiment the author committed to running and has not run. PRED-073 is the only entry where a verification source genuinely has not arrived, and we caveat it accordingly above.

“You are cherry-picking the failures.” The cohort is defined mechanically — every prediction whose window has closed with no dome-posted result — not selected for being unflattering. The complementary set (predictions the dome has claimed) is reviewed point-by-point in Part 3 and Sections 6.1–6.14; the asymmetry is the finding, not a sampling artifact (data/sections.json:p6-612-11; data/sections.json:part3).

“Silence is not the same as a wrong answer.” Correct, and we do not score silence as a falsification on its own. We score each prediction on its physics (seven restate standard physics, two are tacit withdrawals, one is falsified on the dome's own rule). The silent-ignore point is narrower and is about bookkeeping integrity: a scoreboard that can only increment the win column is not a scoreboard, and the reader deserves to know that the dome's win tally is computed over a process that never records a loss.

Cross-references: Section 6.11 (first 0-for-N count, data/sections.json:p6-611-10), Section 6.12 (April closure cluster, data/sections.json:p6-612-11), the Timestamp Error tab (OTS anchors observations, not predictions — the same one-directional accounting problem at the cryptographic layer), and Part 3 (point-by-point review of claimed wins, data/sections.json:part3).
